summary: The root سبط (sbT) primarily describes something lank or straight, especially hair, as opposed to curly. It can also refer to a person who is tall, well-proportioned, or has long fingers.
lane: سَبِطٌ ذ and and , (the first and third of these in one copy of the S, and the second alone in another copy of the S, and all in the M and Msb and K,) the first of the dial. of El- Hijáz, (TA,) from سَبِطَ , and the second from سَبُطَ , the last being an inf. n. used as an epithet, (Msb,) Lank, not crisp; (S, M, * Msb, K; *) applied to hair: (S, Msb:) pl. سِبَاطٌ , which is said by Sb to be of the measure most common for a pl. of an epithet of the measure فَعَلٌ , (M,) or فَعْلٌ . (TA.) -b2- سَبِطُ الشَّعَرِ , (S, M,) and , (M,) A man having lank hair: (S, M:) and in like manner سِبَاطٌ , alone, applied to a number of persons. (TA.) is also metonymically applied to (tropical:) A foreigner, like as [its contr.] جَعْدٌ is to an Arab. (TA.) -b3- سَبِطٌ also signifies Tall; (M, K;) applied to a man: (M:) or, as also , (TA,) or سَبِطُ الجِسْمِ , (M,) so applied, long in the [ bones called ] أَلْوَاح [pl. of لَوْح ], (M, TA,] and even therein: (TA:) or سَبِطُ الجِسْمِ or , (accord. to different copies of the K,) or both, (S, TA,) goodly in stature, or person, or proportion, (S, K,) and evenness. (S.) Also Having extended limbs, and perfect in make. (TA.) And سَبِطُ القَصَبِ , and , A man [ long and even, or] extended, and without protuberances, in the bones of the fore arms and the shanks. (TA.) And سَبِطُ البَنَانِ and , (tropical:) Long in the fingers. (TA.) And سَبِطُ الخَلْقِ A man lank in make: (L in art. رد :) and سَبِطَةُ الخَلْقِ , and , (tropical:) a woman lank, or soft, or tender, in make. (M, Z, TA.) And سَبِطُ السَّاقَيْنِ A man soft, or flaccid, or uncompact, in the shanks. (Ham p. 238.) -b4- اليَدَيْنِ , (M, K, TA,) and سَبِطُهُمَا , (TA, and so in the CK,) and سَبِطُ الكَفَّيْنِ , (TA,) (tropical:) A man who is liberal, bountiful, or munificent. (M, K, TA.) And سَبِطٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ (tropical:) A man easy, or facile, in beneficence. (M, TA.) -b5- مَطَرٌ سَبِطٌ , (Sh, TA,) and , (Sh, K,) (tropical:) Rain pouring abundantly and extensively, (Sh, K,) and consecutively. (Sh, TA.)

headwords.def: اسبط He (a man, S, M) extended himself, or became extended or stretched, (S, M, K, TA,) upon the ground, (S, TA), in consequence of being beaten, (M, K, TA,) &c.: (TA:) he fell (M, K, TA) upon the ground, (TA,) and was unable to move, (M, K, TA,) by reason of weakness, (M, TA,) or from drinking medicine, or some other cause; on the authority of AZ: (M:) he fell upon the ground, and became extended or stretched, in consequence of being beaten, or from disease, and in like manner from drinking medicine. (TA.) And اسبط بِالأَرْضِ He clave to the ground. (Ibn-Jebeleh, M, K.) He was silent, by reason of fear, or fright: (M, L, K:) he was silent and still; or he lowered his eyes, looking towards the ground, and was still. (O.) اسبط فِى نَوْمِهِ

headwords.def: سِبْطٌ A grandchild; (S, Msb, K;) a son's child, and a daughter's child: (M, TA:) pl. أَسْبَاطٌ ; (S, Msb, TA;) which is commonly used by the vulgar as signifying daughters' children; distinguished by them from أَحْفَادٌ [which they apply to son's children, pl. of حَفِيدٌ ]; but the leading lexicologists expressly declare that it includes sons' children and daughters' children, as it is said to do by ISd: IAar explained سِبْطٌ and سِبْطَانِ and أَسْبَاطٌ as signifying the particularly distinguished, and choicest, of children. headwords.def: سُبَاطٌ (AA, S, M, K) and سُبَاطُ , being perfectly and imperfectly decl., (AA, K,) and also written with ش , (TA, and K in art. شبط , ) The name of a month in Greek; (S;) a certain month, [ next ] before آذَارُ ; (K;) the month that is between the winter and the spring; (M;) [ the fifth month of the Syrian year, corresponding with February O. S.; ] it is in the winter-quarters, and in it is the completion of the day whereof the fractions circulate in the years: when the said day is complete in that month, the people of Syria call that year عَامُ الكَبِيسِ ; and when a child is born, or a person arrives from a country, in that year, they consider it fortunate. headwords.def: سُبَاطَةٌ Sweepings, syn. كُنَاسَةٌ , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) which are thrown every day in the courts of houses. (K.) Also A place in which sweepings (Mgh, TA) and dirt (TA) are thrown: occuring in a trad., (Mgh, TA,) and so expl. by El-Khattábee: (Mgh:) but some assign to it there the former meaning. (TA.) [It should be observed that كُنَاسَةٌ also is said to have both these meanings.] Also What falls from, or of, hair when it is combed. (M, TA.) A raceme of a palm-tree, with its fruit-stalks ( عَرَاجِين ) and its fresh ripe dates: of the dial. of Egypt. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: A roof; between two walls; between two houses
headwords.def: سَابَاطٌ A roof (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) between two walls, (S,) or between two houses, (M, K,) having beneath it a road, or way, or passage, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) which is a thoroughfare: (Mgh:) pl. سَوَابِيطُ (S, Msb, K) and سَابَاطَاتٌ . (S, K.)
